question: Does stating the existing schema v2 size limits in the prompt raise first-attempt schema validity without new integrity failures or a material loss of grounding or completeness?

prompt_difference.appended_text:
Size limits:
- At most 4 claims.
- Each claim text: at most 400 characters.
- Each limitation text: at most 300 characters.
- An output that exceeds any of these limits is invalid. Do not exceed them.
- If the evidence holds more than 4 distinct findings, combine semantically related evidence into one claim and cite all of its items.
- Keep materially distinct evidence. Do not drop evidence only to fit a limit when it can be combined with related evidence.
- Prefer concise wording. Do not invent extra claims.

retry_policy: one initial generation; one retry only if the output does not parse into schema v2, with the parser error shown. No retry for wrong, weak, incomplete or abstaining answers. Transport retries (at most 2) re-send a request only when no response was received.
pairing: Each question goes through the frozen v2 pipeline once per condition, A then B. Retrieval is run twice per question before any call and must agree. After both calls, the two records must have the same retrieval item IDs in the same order and the same context_sha256, or the run stops. Only the system prompt differs.

metrics.primary: first-attempt schema validity: schema-valid initial responses / all initial responses, per condition. Never replaced by final validity. A system abstention (empty context) has no initial response and is excluded from the denominator.
secondary: claim_count, claim_length, limitation_length and other violations on first attempts (from the parser error; one attempt can have several)
metrics.semantic: rubric v2 under the context-only evidence boundary (amendment 2026-10-01): claim support, completeness, context sufficiency, abstention, limitations. metrics_v2 per condition, after the owner's blind review is complete and frozen.

definitions.cap_violations_B: B first attempts with at least one claim_count, claim_length or limitation_length violation
definitions.integrity_failures: outputs with any deterministic validation violation, or status rejected_citation or context_invalid
definitions.material_human_regression (impl): B is worse than A by at least 2 on any of: grounded outputs, UNSUPPORTED statements, PARTIAL or INSUFFICIENT completeness judgments, incorrect or missed abstentions (8 questions, so a difference of 1 is treated as noise)

rules: FORMAT_GROUNDING_TRADEOFF: first_valid B > A, and a material human regression
SCHEMA_AWARENESS: first_valid B > A, cap_violations_B <= 1, integrity_failures B <= A, and no material human regression
SCHEMA_CAPACITY_CONFIRMED: cap_violations_B >= 3 of 8 (B still often breaks the caps it was told)
comparison_rule.frozen: not changed after any output exists

blind_review.hidden: condition, prompt name, call order and format outcome
